parts.label: (a)
hints: Write out the law of total probability for a defective component by summing the two machine pathways: $P(\text{Defective}) = P(A \cap \text{Defective}) + P(B \cap \text{Defective})$.
Apply the conditional probability definition in reverse: $P(A \mid \text{Defective}) = \frac{P(A \cap \text{Defective})}{P(\text{Defective})}$, substituting the known branch probabilities.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of drawing a defective item produced by Machine $A$:
$$P(A \cap \text{Def}) = P(A) \times P(\text{Def} \mid A) = 0.60 \times 0.05 = 0.030$$

Calculate the probability of drawing a defective item produced by Machine $B$:
$$P(B \cap \text{Def}) = P(B) \times P(\text{Def} \mid B) = 0.40 \times 0.10 = 0.040$$

Sum both disjoint paths to find the total probability that a chosen item is defective:
$$P(\text{Def}) = 0.030 + 0.040 = 0.070$$

Divide the favorable pathway by the total probability of a defective component:
$$P(A \mid \text{Def}) = \frac{P(A \cap \text{Def})}{P(\text{Def})} = \frac{0.030}{0.070} = \frac{3}{7} \approx 0.429$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the prior machine probabilities and branch defect rates:
$$P(A) = 0.60,\quad P(B) = 0.40,\quad P(\text{Def} \mid A) = 0.05,\quad P(\text{Def} \mid B) = 0.10$$

Determine the joint branch probabilities along each tree branch:
$$P(A \cap \text{Def}) = 0.60 \times 0.05 = 0.03,\quad P(B \cap \text{Def}) = 0.40 \times 0.10 = 0.04$$

Compute the total probability forming the denominator:
$$P(\text{Def}) = 0.03 + 0.04 = 0.07$$

Invert the conditional probability to find the posterior:
$$P(A \mid \text{Def}) = \frac{0.03}{0.07} = \frac{3}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate $P(\text{defective}) = 0.60 \times 0.05 + 0.40 \times 0.10 = 0.07$ or set up the ratio $\frac{0.03}{0.03 + 0.04}$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{3}{7}$ (or $0.429$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Identify the two ways a bus can be late: either it rains and the bus is late, or it is dry and the bus is late: $P(\text{Late}) = P(\text{Rain} \cap \text{Late}) + P(\text{Dry} \cap \text{Late})$.
Compute the numerator $P(\text{Rain} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.3 \times 0.6$ and divide by the total probability of being late.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability that it rains and the bus is late:
$$P(\text{Rain} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$$

Calculate the probability that it is dry and the bus is late:
$$P(\text{Dry} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.7 \times 0.1 = 0.07$$

Find the total probability that the bus arrives late on a randomly chosen morning:
$$P(\text{Late}) = 0.18 + 0.07 = 0.25$$

Apply the conditional probability formula to find the posterior probability of rain:
$$P(\text{Rain} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(\text{Rain} \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})} = \frac{0.18}{0.25} = \frac{18}{25} = 0.72$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Extract the branch probabilities from the problem statement:
$$P(\text{Rain}) = 0.3,\quad P(\text{Dry}) = 0.7,\quad P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Rain}) = 0.6,\quad P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Dry}) = 0.1$$

Calculate the two branch products leading to a late arrival:
$$P(\text{Rain} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18,\quad P(\text{Dry} \cap \text{Late}) = 0.7 \times 0.1 = 0.07$$

Sum to obtain the denominator representing the total late probability:
$$P(\text{Late}) = 0.18 + 0.07 = 0.25$$

Form the inverted conditional ratio:
$$P(\text{Rain} \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{0.18}{0.25} = \frac{18}{25} = 0.72$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluate total probability of late bus as $0.3 \times 0.6 + 0.7 \times 0.1 = 0.25$ and identify numerator as $0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$.
Obtain $\frac{18}{25}$ or $0.72$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Note the sequential structure: passing can occur immediately on attempt 1, or after failing attempt 1 and passing attempt 2: $P(\text{Pass}) = P(\text{Pass}_1) + P(\text{Fail}_1 \cap \text{Pass}_2)$.
Evaluate the favorable path $P(\text{Fail}_1 \cap \text{Pass}_2) = 0.3 \times 0.6$ and divide by $P(\text{Pass})$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the probability of passing on the first attempt directly:
$$P(\text{Pass}_1) = 0.7$$

Determine the probability of failing the first test and passing the second test:
$$P(\text{Fail}_1 \cap \text{Pass}_2) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$$

Calculate the overall probability that the candidate passes the test:
$$P(\text{Pass}) = 0.7 + 0.18 = 0.88$$

Divide the probability of passing on the second attempt by the overall passing probability:
$$P(\text{Pass}_2 \mid \text{Pass}) = \frac{0.18}{0.88} = \frac{18}{88} = \frac{9}{44} \approx 0.205$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the sequential tree branches with unequal lengths:
$$P(\text{Pass}_1) = 0.7,\quad P(\text{Fail}_1) = 1 - 0.7 = 0.3$$

Trace the path to passing on the second attempt:
$$P(\text{Fail}_1 \cap \text{Pass}_2) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$$

Sum all paths resulting in eventual success to find the condition:
$$P(\text{Pass}) = 0.7 + 0.18 = 0.88$$

Calculate the inverted probability that success was achieved on attempt 2:
$$P(\text{2nd attempt} \mid \text{Pass}) = \frac{0.18}{0.88} = \frac{9}{44}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Find total probability of passing as $0.7 + 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.88$ with numerator $0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{9}{44}$ (or $0.205$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Calculate the total probability of selecting a faulty item by summing the fault rates across all three production lines: $P(\text{Fault}) = \sum P(\text{Line}) \times P(\text{Fault} \mid \text{Line})$.
The required posterior probability is $P(Y \mid \text{Fault}) = \frac{P(Y \cap \text{Fault})}{P(\text{Fault})}$. Substitute the values to find the exact fraction.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the joint probability of producing a faulty item on Line $X$:
$$P(X \cap \text{Fault}) = 0.50 \times 0.02 = 0.010$$

Calculate the joint probability of producing a faulty item on Line $Y$:
$$P(Y \cap \text{Fault}) = 0.30 \times 0.04 = 0.012$$

Calculate the joint probability of producing a faulty item on Line $Z$:
$$P(Z \cap \text{Fault}) = 0.20 \times 0.05 = 0.010$$

Sum the three joint probabilities to find the total probability of a faulty item:
$$P(\text{Fault}) = 0.010 + 0.012 + 0.010 = 0.032$$

Evaluate the posterior probability that the faulty item originated from Line $Y$:
$$P(Y \mid \text{Fault}) = \frac{0.012}{0.032} = \frac{12}{32} = \frac{3}{8} = 0.375$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Write down the three prior output shares and their respective defect probabilities:
$$P(X) = 0.5,\; P(Y) = 0.3,\; P(Z) = 0.2;\quad P(F \mid X) = 0.02,\; P(F \mid Y) = 0.04,\; P(F \mid Z) = 0.05$$

Compute the numerator for Line $Y$:
$$P(Y \cap F) = 0.30 \times 0.04 = 0.012$$

Sum all three branches for the denominator:
$$P(F) = (0.50 \times 0.02) + (0.30 \times 0.04) + (0.20 \times 0.05) = 0.010 + 0.012 + 0.010 = 0.032$$

Form the ratio to invert the condition:
$$P(Y \mid F) = \frac{0.012}{0.032} = \frac{3}{8}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate total probability of faulty item $P(\text{faulty}) = 0.5 \times 0.02 + 0.3 \times 0.04 + 0.2 \times 0.05 = 0.032$ with numerator $0.3 \times 0.04 = 0.012$.

parts.label: (a)
hints: Find the conditional probability of receiving no discount for each payment method: $P(\text{No Disc} \mid \text{Cash}) = 1.0$, $P(\text{No Disc} \mid \text{Card}) = 0.90$, and $P(\text{No Disc} \mid \text{App}) = 0.80$.

The numerator requires the union of two distinct payment methods with no discount: $P((\text{Card} \cup \text{App}) \cap \text{No Disc}) = P(\text{Card} \cap \text{No Disc}) + P(\text{App} \cap \text{No Disc})$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of paying by cash and receiving no discount:
$$P(\text{Cash} \cap \text{No Disc}) = 0.2 \times 1.0 = 0.20$$

Calculate the probability of paying by card and receiving no discount:
$$P(\text{Card} \cap \text{No Disc}) = 0.5 \times 0.90 = 0.45$$

Calculate the probability of paying by mobile app and receiving no discount:
$$P(\text{App} \cap \text{No Disc}) = 0.3 \times 0.80 = 0.24$$

Sum the three branches to obtain the total probability of receiving no discount:
$$P(\text{No Disc}) = 0.20 + 0.45 + 0.24 = 0.89$$

Sum the card and app paths in the numerator and divide by the total probability:
$$P(\text{Card or App} \mid \text{No Disc}) = \frac{0.45 + 0.24}{0.89} = \frac{0.69}{0.89} = \frac{69}{89} \approx 0.775$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Establish the complement probabilities of no discount for each branch:
$$P(D' \mid \text{Cash}) = 1 - 0 = 1.0,\quad P(D' \mid \text{Card}) = 1 - 0.10 = 0.90,\quad P(D' \mid \text{App}) = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80$$

Calculate the joint probabilities along all branches:
$$P(\text{Cash} \cap D') = 0.20,\quad P(\text{Card} \cap D') = 0.45,\quad P(\text{App} \cap D') = 0.24$$

Find the total probability of no discount:
$$P(D') = 0.20 + 0.45 + 0.24 = 0.89$$

Combine the electronic payment branches in the numerator:
$$P(\text{Card or App} \mid D') = \frac{0.45 + 0.24}{0.89} = \frac{69}{89}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate total probability of no discount as $0.2 \times 1.0 + 0.5 \times 0.90 + 0.3 \times 0.80 = 0.89$ and combine card and mobile app in numerator as $0.45 + 0.24 = 0.69$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{69}{89}$ (or $0.775$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Break down the population into two disjoint groups: having the condition ($2\%$) and healthy ($98\%$): $P(D) = 0.02,\; P(D') = 0.98$.
Calculate the two ways of receiving a positive test result: a true positive ($0.02 \times 0.90$) and a false positive ($0.98 \times 0.05$).

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of a person having the condition and testing positive:
$$P(D \cap +) = 0.02 \times 0.90 = 0.018$$

Calculate the probability of a person not having the condition and testing positive:
$$P(D' \cap +) = 0.98 \times 0.05 = 0.049$$

Find the total probability of obtaining a positive test result:
$$P(+) = 0.018 + 0.049 = 0.067$$

Evaluate the posterior probability that a person testing positive actually has the condition:
$$P(D \mid +) = \frac{P(D \cap +)}{P(+)} = \frac{0.018}{0.067} = \frac{18}{67} \approx 0.269$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State the prior and conditional parameters:
$$P(D) = 0.02,\quad P(D') = 0.98,\quad P(+ \mid D) = 0.90,\quad P(+ \mid D') = 0.05$$

Compute the numerator representing the true positive branch:
$$P(D \cap +) = 0.02 \times 0.90 = 0.018$$

Compute the total positive rate for the denominator:
$$P(+) = (0.02 \times 0.90) + (0.98 \times 0.05) = 0.018 + 0.049 = 0.067$$

Calculate the posterior probability:
$$P(D \mid +) = \frac{0.018}{0.067} = \frac{18}{67}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Find total positive rate as $0.02 \times 0.90 + 0.98 \times 0.05 = 0.018 + 0.049 = 0.067$ with numerator $0.018$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{18}{67}$ (or $0.269$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Identify the two pathways to acceptance: applying for Engineering and being accepted, or applying for Science and being accepted: $P(\text{Acc}) = P(E \cap \text{Acc}) + P(S \cap \text{Acc})$.
Multiply along each branch and sum: $P(\text{Acc}) = (0.60 \times 0.35) + (0.40 \times 0.50)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of an applicant applying for Engineering and being accepted:
$$P(E \cap \text{Acc}) = P(E) \times P(\text{Acc} \mid E) = 0.60 \times 0.35 = 0.21$$

Calculate the probability of an applicant applying for Science and being accepted:
$$P(S \cap \text{Acc}) = P(S) \times P(\text{Acc} \mid S) = 0.40 \times 0.50 = 0.20$$

Sum the two disjoint probabilities to find the overall acceptance rate:
$$P(\text{Acc}) = 0.21 + 0.20 = 0.41$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the given probabilities for each branch:
$$P(E) = 0.60,\quad P(S) = 0.40,\quad P(\text{Acc} \mid E) = 0.35,\quad P(\text{Acc} \mid S) = 0.50$$

Apply the law of total probability across both disciplines:
$$P(\text{Acc}) = (0.60 \times 0.35) + (0.40 \times 0.50)$$

Evaluate the arithmetic:
$$P(\text{Acc}) = 0.21 + 0.20 = 0.41$$

ai_rubric.observable: Use law of total probability with correct branch products: $0.60 \times 0.35 + 0.40 \times 0.50$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Recall the definition of conditional probability: $P(E \mid \text{Acc}) = \frac{P(E \cap \text{Acc})}{P(\text{Acc})}$.
Use the branch probability $P(E \cap \text{Acc}) = 0.21$ and the total probability from part (a) $P(\text{Acc}) = 0.41$.

walkthrough.text:
Retrieve the joint probability of applying for Engineering and being accepted:
$$P(E \cap \text{Acc}) = 0.21$$

Retrieve the total probability of acceptance from part (a):
$$P(\text{Acc}) = 0.41$$

Compute the conditional probability:
$$P(E \mid \text{Acc}) = \frac{P(E \cap \text{Acc})}{P(\text{Acc})} = \frac{0.21}{0.41} = \frac{21}{41} \approx 0.512$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State the formula for reversing the conditional probability:
$$P(E \mid \text{Acc}) = \frac{P(E \cap \text{Acc})}{P(\text{Acc})}$$

Substitute the numerator and denominator from part (a):
$$P(E \mid \text{Acc}) = \frac{0.21}{0.41}$$

Simplify to an irreducible fraction:
$$P(E \mid \text{Acc}) = \frac{21}{41}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Use Bayes inversion formula $\frac{0.60 \times 0.35}{0.41}$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{21}{41}$ (or $0.512$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Each bag is chosen with probability $1/2$. Find the fraction of red counters in each bag: Bag $X$ has $3/8$ and Bag $Y$ has $6/8$.
Sum the two products: $P(R) = P(\text{Heads}) \times P(R \mid X) + P(\text{Tails}) \times P(R \mid Y)$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the probabilities of selecting each bag:
$$P(X) = \frac{1}{2},\quad P(Y) = \frac{1}{2}$$

Determine the conditional probability of drawing red from Bag $X$ and Bag $Y$:
$$P(R \mid X) = \frac{3}{8},\quad P(R \mid Y) = \frac{6}{8}$$

Calculate the total probability of drawing a red counter:
$$P(R) = \left(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{8}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{6}{8}\right) = \frac{3}{16} + \frac{6}{16} = \frac{9}{16} = 0.5625$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the tree branches for coin toss followed by counter colour:
$$P(X) = \frac{1}{2},\; P(Y) = \frac{1}{2};\quad P(R \mid X) = \frac{3}{8},\; P(R \mid Y) = \frac{6}{8}$$

Calculate the total red probability:
$$P(R) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{8} + \frac{6}{8}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{9}{8} = \frac{9}{16}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up sum of products for red counter: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{8} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{6}{8}$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: First determine the probability of drawing a blue counter from each bag: $P(B \mid X) = 5/8$ and $P(B \mid Y) = 2/8$.
Use Bayes' theorem to reverse the condition: $P(X \mid B) = \frac{P(X \cap B)}{P(B)}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the probability of selecting Bag $X$ and drawing a blue counter:
$$P(X \cap B) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{5}{16}$$

Determine the probability of selecting Bag $Y$ and drawing a blue counter:
$$P(Y \cap B) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{2}{16}$$

Sum to find the total probability of drawing a blue counter:
$$P(B) = \frac{5}{16} + \frac{2}{16} = \frac{7}{16}$$

Evaluate the conditional probability that Bag $X$ was chosen given a blue counter was drawn:
$$P(X \mid B) = \frac{P(X \cap B)}{P(B)} = \frac{5/16}{7/16} = \frac{5}{7} \approx 0.714$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the conditional blue probabilities from each bag:
$$P(B \mid X) = 1 - \frac{3}{8} = \frac{5}{8},\quad P(B \mid Y) = 1 - \frac{6}{8} = \frac{2}{8}$$

Compute the numerator for Bag $X$:
$$P(X \cap B) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{5}{16}$$

Compute the denominator:
$$P(B) = 1 - P(R) = 1 - \frac{9}{16} = \frac{7}{16}$$

Evaluate the posterior probability:
$$P(X \mid B) = \frac{5/16}{7/16} = \frac{5}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify conditional blue branch probabilities $\frac{5}{8}$ for Bag $X$ and $\frac{2}{8}$ for Bag $Y$.
Calculate total blue probability $P(B) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{8} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{8} = \frac{7}{16}$.
Evaluate $\frac{5/16}{7/16}$ to obtain exact fraction $\frac{5}{7}$ (or $0.714$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Identify the two disjoint ways to clear the stage: clearing on attempt 1, or failing attempt 1 and clearing on attempt 2.
Set up the tree calculation: $P(\text{Clear}) = P(C_1) + P(F_1 \cap C_2)$.
Substitute the values $P(C_1) = 0.4$ and $P(F_1 \cap C_2) = (1 - 0.4) \times 0.7$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the probability of clearing on the first attempt directly:
$$P(C_1) = 0.4$$

Calculate the probability of failing the first attempt:
$$P(F_1) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$$

Calculate the joint probability of failing the first attempt and clearing on the second attempt:
$$P(F_1 \cap C_2) = 0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42$$

Sum the two mutually exclusive winning outcomes:
$$P(\text{Clear}) = 0.4 + 0.42 = 0.82$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Structure the stopping tree diagram:
$$P(\text{Pass}_1) = 0.4,\quad P(\text{Fail}_1) = 0.6$$

Calculate the two-attempt success route:
$$P(\text{Fail}_1 \cap \text{Pass}_2) = 0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42$$

Combine to find the overall clearance probability:
$$P(\text{Clear}) = 0.40 + 0.42 = 0.82$$

ai_rubric.observable: Apply addition of disjoint successful routes: $0.4 + 0.6 \times 0.7$.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Notice the condition: we are given that the player cleared the stage, so the sample space is restricted to $P(\text{Clear}) = 0.82$.
Failing on the first attempt while clearing means clearing specifically on the second attempt: $P(F_1 \cap \text{Clear}) = P(F_1 \cap C_2)$.
Apply the conditional formula: $P(F_1 \mid \text{Clear}) = \frac{P(F_1 \cap C_2)}{P(\text{Clear})}$, using values from part (a).

walkthrough.text:
Identify the event that the player failed on their first attempt and cleared the stage:
$$P(F_1 \cap \text{Clear}) = P(F_1 \cap C_2) = 0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42$$

Retrieve the total probability of clearing from part (a):
$$P(\text{Clear}) = 0.82$$

Evaluate the conditional probability:
$$P(F_1 \mid \text{Clear}) = \frac{0.42}{0.82} = \frac{42}{82} = \frac{21}{41} \approx 0.512$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Express the conditional event formally:
$$P(F_1 \mid \text{Clear}) = \frac{P(F_1 \cap \text{Clear})}{P(\text{Clear})}$$

Substitute the two-attempt clearance probability as the numerator:
$$P(F_1 \cap C_2) = 0.42$$

Divide by the total clearance probability and simplify:
$$P(F_1 \mid \text{Clear}) = \frac{0.42}{0.82} = \frac{21}{41}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify that clearing after failing the first attempt corresponds to the route Fail on 1st then Pass on 2nd with probability $0.6 \times 0.7 = 0.42$.
Set up conditional probability quotient $\frac{0.42}{0.82}$.
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{21}{41}$ (or $0.512$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Find the on-time probability for each delivery service by taking the complement of late delivery: $1 - P(\text{Late})$.
Compute the on-time probabilities: $P(\text{On time} \mid E) = 0.96$, $P(\text{On time} \mid S) = 0.92$, and $P(\text{On time} \mid B) = 0.85$.
Sum the products of service share and on-time probability: $P(\text{On time}) = (0.45 \times 0.96) + (0.35 \times 0.92) + (0.20 \times 0.85)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the conditional on-time probabilities for all three services:
$$P(T \mid E) = 1 - 0.04 = 0.96,\quad P(T \mid S) = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92,\quad P(T \mid B) = 1 - 0.15 = 0.85$$

Calculate the joint probability of on-time delivery for each service:
$$P(E \cap T) = 0.45 \times 0.96 = 0.432,\quad P(S \cap T) = 0.35 \times 0.92 = 0.322,\quad P(B \cap T) = 0.20 \times 0.85 = 0.170$$

Sum the three joint probabilities to find the overall on-time probability:
$$P(T) = 0.432 + 0.322 + 0.170 = 0.924$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Write down the three branch probabilities and on-time complements:
$$P(E) = 0.45,\; P(S) = 0.35,\; P(B) = 0.20;\quad P(T \mid E) = 0.96,\; P(T \mid S) = 0.92,\; P(T \mid B) = 0.85$$

Compute the total on-time probability by combining the three paths:
$$P(T) = (0.45 \times 0.96) + (0.35 \times 0.92) + (0.20 \times 0.85)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Deduce on-time conditional probabilities: $0.96$ for Express, $0.92$ for Standard, $0.85$ for Economy.
Compute total on-time probability $0.45 \times 0.96 + 0.35 \times 0.92 + 0.20 \times 0.85$ (or calculate total late probability $0.076$ and subtract from 1).

parts.label: (b)
hints: First find the total probability that a package is delivered late using the result from part (a): $P(\text{Late}) = 1 - P(\text{On time})$.
Calculate the joint probability that a package was sent by Economy and was delivered late: $P(B \cap \text{Late}) = 0.20 \times 0.15$.
Evaluate the conditional probability: $P(B \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(B \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})}$, simplifying the fraction.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the total probability that a package is late using the complement of part (a):
$$P(\text{Late}) = 1 - 0.924 = 0.076$$

Calculate the joint probability of sending by Economy and arriving late:
$$P(B \cap \text{Late}) = 0.20 \times 0.15 = 0.030$$

Apply Bayes' theorem to reverse the condition:
$$P(B \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{P(B \cap \text{Late})}{P(\text{Late})} = \frac{0.030}{0.076} = \frac{30}{76} = \frac{15}{38} \approx 0.395$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the denominator using complement rule:
$$P(\text{Late}) = 1 - 0.924 = 0.076$$

Compute the numerator for Economy:
$$P(B \cap \text{Late}) = 0.20 \times 0.15 = 0.030$$

Form the posterior probability and simplify:
$$P(B \mid \text{Late}) = \frac{0.030}{0.076} = \frac{30}{76} = \frac{15}{38}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate joint late probability for Economy service $P(B \cap \text{Late}) = 0.20 \times 0.15 = 0.030$.
Find total late probability $P(\text{Late}) = 1 - 0.924 = 0.076$ (or evaluate $0.45 \times 0.04 + 0.35 \times 0.08 + 0.20 \times 0.15$).
Obtain exact fraction $\frac{15}{38}$ (or $0.395$ to 3 significant figures).

parts.label: (a)
hints: Partition the school into three grades: $G_{10}$ ($0.30$), $G_{11}$ ($0.45$), and $G_{12}$ ($0.25$).
Multiply each grade proportion by its competition participation rate: $P(M) = \sum P(G_i) \times P(M \mid G_i)$.
Evaluate each product and sum them together to find the overall probability.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the probability of choosing a Grade 10 participant:
$$P(G_{10} \cap M) = 0.30 \times 0.20 = 0.06$$

Calculate the probability of choosing a Grade 11 participant:
$$P(G_{11} \cap M) = 0.45 \times 0.40 = 0.18$$

Calculate the probability of choosing a Grade 12 participant:

Form the conditional probability ratio:

parts.label: (a)
